incidents.title: Criminals build 2FA-bypass zero-day with AI for planned mass exploitation
incidents.targets: Popular open-source web-based system administration tool (unnamed)
incidents.outcome: Exploit disrupted before the planned mass exploitation; vendor notified.
incidents.confidenceReason: GTIG assesses LLM authorship with high confidence from artifacts such as a hallucinated CVSS score; no model is named.
incidents.summary: GTIG found a Python zero-day exploit that bypasses 2FA via a hardcoded trust assumption and believes an AI model helped find and weaponize it. It is GTIG's first identified AI-developed zero-day. Google does not name the group or the product.
incidents.quote: For the first time, GTIG has identified a threat actor using a zero-day exploit that we believe was developed with AI.

incidents.targets: Indonesian government domains, another country's government domain, and private-sector entities
incidents.outcome: Multiple government and private-sector targets compromised.
incidents.confidenceReason: CrowdStrike examined exposed offensive frameworks and documented successful AI-directed intrusions.
incidents.summary: Observed during May–August 2026, the operator supplied Claude Code with 819 skills, primarily from public repositories. Human intervention addressed guardrails and stalled exploitation. The date represents the beginning of the reported observation window; the operation's exact start was not specified.
incidents.quote: The least sophisticated of the four in this report is an Indonesian-speaking actor that uses 819 skills (overwhelmingly sourced from public GitHub repositories, primarily claude-red1) without additional orchestration to enable Claude Code to conduct intrusion campaigns.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only CrowdStrike has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.
